text: A firm must test every change to a system supporting an important business service before the change is released, and must keep a record of the results.
For the purposes of XSYS 4.1.1R, a firm should consider automated regression tests and a test environment that resembles production.
XSYS 4.1.1R does not apply to an emergency change, provided that the firm tests the change within two business days of release and complies with XSYS 4.2.1R.
A firm must ensure that a change is approved by a person other than the person who made it.
Peer review of source code recorded in a version control system may be evidence of approval under XSYS 4.2.1R.
A firm must keep audit logs of access to customer data for at least three years.
A firm must keep audit logs of access to customer data for at least five years.
A firm must ensure that audit logs cannot be altered or deleted by the staff whose access they record.
A firm must not store passwords, keys or other credentials in source code or in any place accessible to unauthorised staff.
A firm must encrypt customer data in transit and at rest.
Before relying on a third-party software supplier, a firm must assess the risk that the supplier's failure would pose to an important business service. See also XSYS 99.1.1R.
A firm must act in good faith towards customers and avoid causing them foreseeable harm.
Customer-facing software that makes cancelling harder than buying is unlikely to be consistent with XPRN 1.1.1R.
